claim:
Let \(n\ge2\), let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) be an unknown Hessian, and let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) be a known gradient. After one exact Hessian-vector observation \(y=Av\) with \(v
e0\), the Newton solve vector \(p=A^{-1}g\) (and hence the conventional Newton step \(-p\)) is uniquely determined over all symmetric positive-definite completions consistent with that observation if and only if \(g\in\operatorname{span}\{y\}\); in that case \(p=lpha v\) for the scalar \(lpha\) satisfying \(g=lpha y\). Consequently, one Hessian-vector observation cannot guarantee exact Newton-direction recovery for every positive-definite quadratic in dimension at least two.

correctness.rationale:
The forward implication follows from \(A^{-1}g=lpha v\) when \(g=lpha Av\). For the converse, use coordinates with \(v=e_1\) and write every SPD completion as \(A_D= egin{psmallmatrix}a&b^{\mathsf T}\b&D\end{psmallmatrix}\), with \(D-bb^{\mathsf T}/a\succ0\). If \(g
otin\operatorname{span}\{y\}\), the orthogonal component of every Newton solution is nonzero; replacing \(D\) by \(D+	au I\) preserves the observed first column but cannot preserve the solution. The exact rational witness verifies this distinction.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary paper proves sufficiency of at most two curvature directions for a recursive subspace quasi-Newton construction. The present claim is a complementary exact classification of when one observed Hessian-vector product uniquely determines the Newton solve vector across all SPD completions. Retrieved published-finding corpus findings on BFGS matrix recovery and curvature estimation address different statements and do not imply this criterion.
residual_risks: Classical information-based complexity literature may contain an equivalent one-Hessian-vector identifiability lemma not surfaced by the searches; no universal priority claim is made.
The result does not quantify conditioning or approximate recovery and does not lower-bound adaptive multi-query methods.

value.rationale: The iff criterion identifies the exact exceptional case where one curvature observation suffices and otherwise proves a universal ambiguity across SPD completions. It is a natural information boundary for methods that seek an exact Newton solve vector without line-search or historical conjugacy information. The explicit rational witness makes the obstruction directly reproducible.
